text:
morgan: FYI rollout of kernel-router v2 landed to canary and we saw 3/12 nodes OOM within ~30m on long-context jobs. holding the rest of the rollout. :warning:

anita: not great — are these the same hosts that hit the prefault spike last week?

morgan: different hosts. pattern looks like big KV allocations + fast prefetch path. heap growth spikes right after first token decode. attaching pmap-ish snapshot next.

morgan: ```
# /proc/<pid>/maps snippet
7f8a0000-7f8c0000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0                          [heap]
...large anon pages aligned with slab hotlists
KV cache: ~1.9GB -> jumps to ~3.7GB in 10s
```

jamie: CI perf-run for kernel-router v2 also showed mem increase on longctx suites, but unit tests passed. perf test: https://ci/reports/1234 (flaky mem chart attached).

ci-bot: perf/regression: longctx-mem-suite increased 38% RSS vs baseline on canary-3 (commit f3a2b1c -> 5f7d2a0).

lee: can we bisect to a smaller commit range? kernel-router v2 had three subchanges: prefetch scheduling, eviction-score tweak, and kernel selection fallback. which landed together?

morgan: landed in one PR but split into 3 commits. suspecting prefetch scheduling + aggressive prefix-reserve. eviction-score tweak shouldn't allocate extra memory. kernel selection fallback changes look unrelated to alloc shape but could change hot paths.

anita: quick mitigation: throttle prefetch (K_PREFETCH_MAX=4) and reduce continuous-batch window to 16. can we flip those remotely? ops-bot can toggle feature flags?

ops-bot: feature flag update applied: PREFETCH_MAX set to 4 on canary cluster. verify.

morgan: after PREFETCH_MAX=4 we still saw two OOMs but they happened later and RSS growth slope reduced by ~40%. looks like prefetch is a contributor but not whole cause.

lee: plan: 1) bisect the 3 commits, 2) reproduce on perf-prod-small with synthetic longctx load, 3) collect jemalloc and KV slab histograms + async stack traces. I can take bisect.

jamie: I kicked off a perf-prod-small run with the same workload. adding jemalloc stats: https://perf/log/5678. Also adding a small script to dump kv-cache stats every 5s: 

```
while true; do curl -s localhost:9001/debug/kv_stats >> kvdump.log; sleep 5; done
```

morgan: bisect result (quick): commit range points to commit 5f7d2a0 which is the prefetch scheduling change. when reverted locally, RSS back to baseline. confirming with local reproduce.

lee: good find. can we craft a narrower revert or a patch to limit prefetch concurrency instead of full revert?

anita: the prefetch path was trying to speed up longctx by pre-reserving K cache slots. bug: we pre-allocated slot arrays sized by prefix_len without considering downstream slab compaction, causing temporary peak allocations. patch ready to cap alloc and yield to evict path.

morgan: patch looks small. test-run shows no OOMs for 2 hours under synthetic load and perf delta ~+1% CPU but stable memory.

sara: decision: hold rollout, apply patch to canary and run 8h smoke. if green, resume gradual rollout with PREFETCH_MAX config lowered by default. I approve revert-only if patch fails.

lee: created PR with fix and test vectors: https://github/repo/pull/987 — marking rollout-hold.

jamie: adding postmortem pointer: remember to include KV slab histograms in CI perf runs for longctx so we catch transient peaks. filing a follow-up ticket.

morgan: thanks everyone. continuing monitor. :thumbsup:
